topic: the measured copy-path floor explains the remaining prefill gap

microbenchmark.note: pure data movement, no arithmetic: 64MB in and 64MB out through UB, per-core contiguous chunks

write_only_TBps.reading: the write path saturates near 1.13 TB/s and does not respond to chunk size at all

copy_TBps_separate_buffers.reading: best aggregate is about 1.73 TB/s and is insensitive to chunk size and pipeline depth

microbenchmark.ub_limit_note: chunk 128KB with stages>=3 and chunk 256KB need dyn_ubuf 393216 B and above and are refused at launch (ACL 107000)

conclusion: our kernel already runs at or slightly below the time a pure copy of the same bytes takes through the TileLang copy path
the vendor moves the same bytes faster than that copy path can, so the residual prefill gap sits in the data-movement path, not in our arithmetic schedule

this is a statement about the measured TileLang copy path on this host; it is not a claim about hardware capability in general, because the vendor evidently uses a path we have not been able to reach from TileLang
status: prefill remains short; decode remains EXCEED at 1.3160x
